Web edition of a lexicon compiled among Raj Mureas at Bhatpal village, Bastar, by Fran Woods and Betsy Schuyler \(1967–1969\) and by Woods on field trips \(1971–1978\)\. Devanagari headwords with phonemic IPA citation forms, English and Hindi definitions, illustrative sentences, SIL semantic\-domain codes and typed variant, complex\-form and cross\-reference relations\. SIL Language \\\\& Culture Archives entry 84724 reported 7,556 entries at publication; the 2026\-08\-26 crawl of the live edition yields 7,788 distinct entry GUIDs\.
URL: [https://www\.webonary\.org/halbi/](https://www.webonary.org/halbi/)\.
references.progress: 7,773 of the 7,788 entries rendered by the vernacular browse index: every record carrying a headword, an IPA citation form, and either a definition or a variant-of relation. Fifteen records are excluded and accounted for in the audit --- 7 with no citation form, 7 with neither definition nor relation, and 1 whose citation-form field holds Devanagari. Example sentences, pictures and audio are not installed

language.name: Gondi
language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="-2 -2 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="14" cy="14" r="13" fill="#98FB98" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

references.source:
David K\. Beine\.
A sociolinguistic survey of the gondi\-speaking communities of central india\.
Master's thesis, San Diego State University, San Diego, 1994\.
Comparative word lists of 210 meanings elicited at 46 survey sites across Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Orissa, transcribed in IPA, with mutual\-intelligibility testing\.
references.progress: The 210-meaning IPA word list for each of the 46 survey sites, as digitized by Rama, \c{C}\"oltekin and Sofroniev (2017). The thesis itself was not consulted; its prose, sociolinguistic testing, questionnaires and site descriptions beyond the survey-site labels are not represented
references.provenance: Not consulted directly. Every installed form reaches Jambu through the digitization released as rama-coltekin-sofroniev2017gondi; see that entry for checksums and the audit trail

references.source:
Taraka Rama, Çağrı Çöltekin, and Pavel Sofroniev\.
A computational analysis of gondi dialects\.
In *Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on NLP for Similar Languages, Varieties and Dialects \(VarDial\)*, 26–35\. Valencia, Spain, 2017\. Association for Computational Linguistics\.
Digitization of the word lists collected by Beine \(1994\); the survey\-site coordinates are the authors' geolocation of Beine's site descriptions, published in maps/gondi\.kml\.
URL: [https://github\.com/PhyloStar/Gondi\-Dialect\-Analysis](https://github.com/PhyloStar/Gondi-Dialect-Analysis), [doi:10\.5281/zenodo\.1220088](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1220088)\.
references.progress: The complete 46 sites x 210 concepts IPA matrix in data/gondi_combined_cognates.csv, one Jambu form per elicited response. The 158 cells printed as ----- carry no elicited word and are recorded in the audit only. Excludes the LingPy-derived ASJP and SCA recodings, Taraka Rama's Gondi-internal Cognate Class judgments (both preserved per record in the audit), the pre-segmented copy in data/combined_data.tsv, and the Nexus matrices, MrBayes consensus trees, autoencoder code and paper, which are analysis results rather than lexemes. Survey-site names, coordinates and the Glottolog subgroup labels of table 1 are installed as dialect metadata
references.provenance: Upstream repository cloned on 2026-08-25 and pinned at release v1.0; SHA-256 738f3a0bb4045d9c256542176aa18e7a96ba4320faed0061f738827d73162ef7 (data/gondi_combined_cognates.csv), db68fc7e878c3abe31806ab57a5c909ebcae501ece06d8370e0bd3a20a99edf1 (data/gondi_combined.tsv) and 8fac9b91a69c30e3f97148a6ca3e70a1941c44c4a66915e656107a64b362cbbb (maps/gondi.kml), each byte-identical at v1.0 and at master 642425c. Reproducible importer data/other/forms/raw_data/gondi_beine.py with the checked-in audit data/other/forms/raw_data/20260825-gondi-beine-audit.csv, manifest 20260825-gondi-beine-manifest.json and seeded sample 20260825-gondi-beine-sample.csv; installed rows in data/other/forms/20260825-gondi-beine.csv
references.locator: data/gondi_combined_cognates.csv, row 6133, site grp, concept rainbow

SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015\-012, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 2015\.
Printed numeric lexical\-similarity labels remain audit\-only and do not assert historical cognacy\. Seven same\-list cross\-references are resolved deterministically\. Typed audit notes preserve faint, unlabelled and clipped fragments without guessing them into installed forms\. The report names the six localities but gives no point coordinates, so dialect coordinates remain blank\.

The 840 BPL Braj/Haryanvi, PBG Baghati Pahari, HIN Hindustani and PUN Punjabi comparison cells are retained audit-only and are not manually transcribed
references.provenance: Official SIL publisher PDF downloaded 2026-08-28, SHA-256 53121a1b9803ba502092866080e3bdb35457bc6040dcc7f47da508eca1fef2e2; the PDF is not redistributed. references.source:
Bijumon Varghese, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuel\.
The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009\-011\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009-011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix B, printed pages 59--177: 6,894 lexical responses from thirty Malvi target lists grouped by the source as Ujjaini, Rajwadi, Umadwadi, Sondhwadi, Gond-Malvi and Bhil-Malvi. Excludes 37 target cells printed as "By Name" rather than a lexical form, two Bhili and two Nimadi comparison lists, the Bhopali comparison list, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standards, ten explicit no-entry control cells, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine and 24 feces which the report says were disqualified and removed
references.provenance: The exact official publisher PDF was recovered through Internet Archive capture 20150930085157 because the legacy SIL URL no longer serves the file directly; PDF SHA-256 e67e314974ab10eb8244b08dba56d08d1ce8cbf16eaef1be022071d49032a2dd. The PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible font decoding, geometric extraction and checked snapshot are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_malvi_2009; complete per-record audit is data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-malvi-audit.csv; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-malvi.csv
references.locator: Appendix B, printed p. 82, item 50, Ujjaini-Malvi-Harsodan

language.name: Malvi
language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="-2 -2 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="14" cy="14" r="13" fill="#6BCD00" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

references.source:
Bijumon Varghese, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuel\.
The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009\-011\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009-011.pdf)\.

references.source:
Binoy Koshy\.
A sociolinguistic study of bagheli speakers in madhya pradesh\.
Technical Report 2022\-015, SIL International, 2022\.
The report was created in 2004 and published in 2022\. All eighteen target lects attach to canonical Bagheli\. Similarity\-group numbers remain source notes and are not treated as historical cognacy\. Two readable forms lacking any printed site code remain excluded, one source\-questioned form is installed without punctuation but explicitly annotated, and one uppercase site code is interpreted conservatively at medium confidence\. The report names localities but supplies no defensible historical collection coordinates\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/resources/archives/94596](https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/94596)\.

language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="-2 -2 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="14" cy="14" r="13" fill="#ff9a00" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

origin_lemma.etymology: 9349 bhaginī f. 'sister' Mn., °nikā- f. Kathās. [J. Gonda AO xxi 23 supports derivation from bhaga-² 'vulva' (which, if it belongs to the 'crooked' or 'defective' word-groups of bhaṅgurá- or *vaṅka-², might with a variant *bagha- account for *baghinī- ~ bhaginī-). But EWA ii 460 sees in it more prob. the feminine of bhagín- as an expression of good wish — bhágaḥ kanī́nām of RV. i 163, 8 — to an unwed sister (note that in NIA. bhaginī- is usu. the younger sister). The transference of aspiration from the initial to the interior presents difficulty, unless as a conscious avoidance of similarity with bhaga-² 'vulva'. The argument in AO xxi 30 that no *baghinī- is attested and that therefore the transference could have occurred only at the stage bhaïṇī- is not conclusive that a form *baghinī- never in fact existed between the age of Aśoka and the first emergence of Pk. bahiṇī-. It is significant that in bhāginēya- no such transference occurred. The new bahiṇī- belonged to the Centre, the older bhaïṇī- remaining on the periphery in Dard., S., L., P., some WH. dialects, EA., Or., and Ko. — For distribution of svásr̥- and bhaginī- in NIA. see AO xxi 27. — bhagín-]

Gonda AO xxi 23 supports derivation from bhaga-² 'vulva' (which, if it belongs to the 'crooked' or 'defective' word-groups of bhaṅgurá- or *vaṅka-², might with a variant *bagha- account for *baghinī- ~ bhaginī-). But EWA ii 460 sees in it more prob. the feminine of bhagín- as an expression of good wish — bhágaḥ kanī́nām of RV. i 163, 8 — to an unwed sister (note that in NIA. bhaginī- is usu. the younger sister). The transference of aspiration from the initial to the interior presents difficulty, unless as a conscious avoidance of similarity with bhaga-² 'vulva'. The argument in AO xxi 30 that no *baghinī- is attested and that therefore the transference could have occurred only at the stage bhaïṇī- is not conclusive that a form *baghinī- never in fact existed between the age of Aśoka and the first emergence of Pk. bahiṇī-. It is significant that in bhāginēya- no such transference occurred. The new bahiṇī- belonged to the Centre, the older bhaïṇī- remaining on the periphery in Dard., S., L., P., some WH. dialects, EA., Or., and Ko. — For distribution of svásr̥- and bhaginī- in NIA. see AO xxi 27. — bhagín-]

references.source:
Fran Woods\.
Halbi – english dictionary\.
Webonary\.org, 2019\.
Web edition of a lexicon compiled among Raj Mureas at Bhatpal village, Bastar, by Fran Woods and Betsy Schuyler \(1967–1969\) and by Woods on field trips \(1971–1978\)\. Devanagari headwords with phonemic IPA citation forms, English and Hindi definitions, illustrative sentences, SIL semantic\-domain codes and typed variant, complex\-form and cross\-reference relations\. SIL Language \\\\& Culture Archives entry 84724 reported 7,556 entries at publication; the 2026\-08\-26 crawl of the live edition yields 7,788 distinct entry GUIDs\.
URL: [https://www\.webonary\.org/halbi/](https://www.webonary.org/halbi/)\.
references.progress: 7,773 of the 7,788 entries rendered by the vernacular browse index: every record carrying a headword, an IPA citation form, and either a definition or a variant-of relation. Fifteen records are excluded and accounted for in the audit --- 7 with no citation form, 7 with neither definition nor relation, and 1 whose citation-form field holds Devanagari. Example sentences, pictures and audio are not installed

The survey combines wordlists elicited during 1998 fieldwork with lists reused from earlier Bhil\-country, Dhule, Garasia, Dungra Bhil and Ahirani studies\. Source lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\.
